title: Contextual Online Uncertainty-Aware Preference Learning for Human Feedback
abstract: arXiv:2504.19342v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has become a pivotal paradigm in artificial intelligence to align large models with human preferences. In this paper, we propose a novel statistical framework to simultaneously conduct the online decision-making and statistical inference on the optimal model using human preference data based on dynamic contextual information. Our approach introduces an efficient decision strategy that achieves both the optimal regret bound and the asymptotic distribution of the estimators. A key challenge in RLHF is handling the dependent online human preference outcomes with dynamic contexts. To address this, in the methodological aspect, we propose a two-stage algorithm starting with $\epsilon$-greedy followed by exploitations; in the theoretical aspect, we tailor anti-concentration inequalities and matrix martingale concentration techniques to derive the uniform estimation rate and asymptotic

translated_title: 基于上下文的不确定性感知在线人类反馈偏好学习
translated_abstract: 从人类反馈中进行强化学习（RLHF）已成为人工智能中将大型模型与人类偏好对齐的关键范式。本文提出了一种新颖的统计框架，利用基于动态上下文信息的人类偏好数据，同时进行在线决策制定和最优模型的统计推断。我们的方法引入了一种高效的决策策略，该策略同时实现了最优遗憾界和估计量的渐近分布。RLHF中的一个关键挑战是处理具有动态上下文的依赖在线人类偏好结果。为解决这一问题，在方法论方面，我们提出了一种两阶段算法，从ε-贪心开始，随后进行利用；在理论方面，我们定制了反集中不等式和矩阵鞅集中技术，以推导均匀估计速率和渐近性。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于上下文的在线不确定性感知偏好学习框架，通过两阶段算法同时实现最优遗憾界和统计推断，有效解决了RLHF中动态上下文下的依赖偏好数据处理难题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a contextual online uncertainty-aware preference learning framework that achieves both optimal regret bounds and statistical inference via a two-stage algorithm, effectively addressing dependent preference outcomes with dynamic contexts in RLHF.
